items.note: End of the article (PDF p. 25, right column, 'gunt mendacium veritati … crucifigens') had been cut into daniel-002-part1.txt; moved back into daniel-001.txt. Margin 'Jer. i, 17' taken as Jer 50:17; Denis says 'as Isaias foretold' of Joakim's burial (Jer 22:19), kept with a note; corrected margins Ps 93:12, Ecclus 31:23, Jdt 8:10, Ps 76:3 (each noted).

(from the Daniel 1 run) The first lines of the old daniel-002-part1.txt, 'gunt mendacium veritati … quotidie crucifigens' (PDF p. 25 right column), are the end of Art. I and are now published there; leave them out of Art. II. | Part 1 published (scheduled run, one worker; Dan 2:1 to mid v. 23). Needs scan of PDF 26 (printed p. 16): the transcription stops after 'Nam et Josephus decimo Antiquitatum libro, Post secundum, inquit,' and the rest of that column is missing (it must have held the v. 1 lemma 'et conterritus est spiritus ejus'); marked […] with a note. Misread margins corrected with notes: 'Eccli. v, 1' = Ecclus 1:1; 'IV Reg. ix, 11' = 4 Kings 20:11; 'Væ terræ cujus rex puer est' is Eccles 10:16 (Denis says Ecclesiasticus). Margin variant notes '* novi' (v. 8), '* deceptione plenam' (v. 9) given as notes. 'perierant' (Jer 10:11) kept as transcribed.

Part 2 published (scheduled run, one worker; mid v. 23 to the end, with the St Francis paragraph). Misread margins corrected with notes: 'Is. ix, 12' = Is 60:12; 'Ps. i, 8' = Ps 50:8; 'Ps. lxxxi, 19' = Ps 71:19; 'Exod. xviii' = Ex 18:11. Ranges Acts 28:3-6, 14:10-12 given single reference-only markers. Denis reads 'præfectum et magistrum' (v. 48) for 'præfectum magistratuum'; margin '* erat' (v. 49) as a note. 'domo succensa' kept as printed.

Margin 'Jer. xxiv, 17' cannot be right (Jer 24 has 10 verses): taken as Jer 24:9, with a note (wording closest to Jer 34:17). Edition reading notes kept at 3:3 (erexerat/posuerat) and 3:26. DR data slip: Dan 3:47 reads 'nine and forth cubits'.

Part 1 of 3 published (scheduled run, two workers split at the v. 56 lemma; Dan 3:49–63, ending with Dan 12:3, whose last words 'erudiunt … æternitates' stand at the top of daniel-004-part2.txt: part 2 should start after them, at the v. 64 lemma). Pages given as pp. 44–69 for the whole article. Lost letters at a page turn: 'Ecclesia mi- / et triumphans' read 'mi[litans]'. Margin numbers corrected with notes: Ps cxlvii, 19 → Ps 147:8; Ps cxiii, 2 → Ps 112:2; Ps lxxxix, 2 → Ps 79:2; Job xliii, 2 → Job 42:2; Job xxxviii, 18 → Job 37:18; 'Deut. xxxii, 27' does not fit 'Manus Domini fecit hæc omnia' (Job 12:9 marked, noted). Prov 10:1 / 13:1 and Ex 25:20, 22 (words of Heb 9:5) reference-only with notes.

Part 2 of 3 published (scheduled run, two workers split at the v. 77 lemma; vv. 64–88, starting after the Dan 12:3 words that end part 1, and ending with the sentence 'Et istud miraculum in Sanctis novi Testamenti … conscribitur', which straddles into daniel-004-part3.txt). Margin numbers corrected with notes: Ps cxlvii, 16/17 → Ps 147:5/6 and Ps cxlvii, 19, 20 → Ps 147:8–9 (Hebrew numbering); Job xxxvii, 35 → Job 38:35; Job xxxviii, 11–13 → Job 37:11–13; Ps lxxxvi, 3 → Ps 76:3 (reference only); Ps. i, 19 → Ps 50:19; 'Job xxxiv' (God on the beasts) → Job 39:1, 'Job xl, xli' → Job 40:20 (reference only). Denis reads 'æstas' for 'æstus' at v. 67 (noted). Augustine's 'decimo de Trinitate' for the Plotinus passage (City of God X, 14) noted. DR data slips: Rom 13:12 'is passed And', Is 12:3 'Thou shall draw'.

Part 3 of 3 published (scheduled run, one worker; from 'Ex quo frivola declaratur instantia Hebræi' to the end: v. 50 again, vv. 89–100, and the question why Daniel is not named, tagged vv. 1, 12). Margin 'v. 94' at 'Tunc Nabuchodonosor rex obstupuit' read as v. 91; 'vers. 3' as a reference-only marker to 3:3. Denis says Deuteronomy for 'Dominum Deum tuum adorabis' (Matthew's wording): Deut 6:13 marked, noted. Variant readings noted: 'Deo solo' (3:95), 'A me ergo rege' (3:96), 'de omni angustia' (Ecclus 51:12); 'catena*' with margin variant 'caterva'. DR data slip: Tob 12:7 lacks 'but honourable'.

Part 1 of 2 published (scheduled run, two workers split at the v. 17 lemma; Dan 4:1 to the Tobias quotation in v. 24, ending '…non patietur animam ire in tenebras'). The last lines of daniel-005-part1.txt, from the lemma '_Forsitan ignoscet Deus delictis tuis._' ('Quum per Ezechielem … omnium ini-'), are NOT translated: part 2 must start there and join them to the top of daniel-005-part2.txt. Pages given as pp. 69–83 for the whole article. Garbled line restored as 'cœpit intra se tacite cogitare, qualiter religio regio culmini servaret honorem' (v. 16); 'hostibus imprimis' kept, noted as perhaps 'imprimi'. Margin 'vers. 12' beside 'germen radicum ejus' marked 4:20 (same words), noted; margin '* pabulum' at v. 20 as a note. Is 29:14/1 Cor 1:19 and Matt 10:19/Luke 21:14 double notes: words quoted marked, the other reference-only. Ecclus 3:33 (old version), Luke 12:37, Luke 10:34, Wis 12:18, Apoc 12:14, Is 37:36 and the Apoc voices reference-only with notes. Ps 72:9 tagged without margin note (Denis cites it with 'itemque').

Start from the lemma '_Forsitan ignoscet Deus delictis tuis._' near the end of daniel-005-part1.txt (its last lines, 'Quum per Ezechielem … omnium ini-', continue at the top of this file); part 1 stops before it. | Part 2 published (scheduled run, one worker; from the v. 24 lemma 'Forsitan ignoscet' to the end). Margin 'v. 23' beside 'Omnia hæc … venerunt' is v. 25 (tagged so). Jer 18:7 and Wis 11:24 marked without margin notes (Denis names the source). Rom 11:33, Jon 3:4, Is 38:1, Gen 2:25, Dan 3:100, Dan 3:27 reference-only. Notes on Denis's readings: transiit (v. 28), sanasti (Tob 11:17), tenebris (1 Pet 1:14), regis (Prov 20:28), 'omnes viæ' (v. 34); Sedulius for 'Sallust'; Art. VI cross-reference. Latin slips fixed: pœnitexeret→pœniteret, rege.fuit, prophéticæ.

End of the article (5:30-31, PDF p. 102 right column, 'Non habitabitur … dignus') had been cut into daniel-007.txt; moved back. Margin 'Jer. i, li' read as Jer. l, li; 'Dan. i, 2' beside the v. 7 cross-reference does not fit (Dan 2:2 used, with a note).

Published (scheduled run, two workers split at the v. 10 lemma). Gen 41:40 marked without margin note (named and word for word). Range notes given one marker each (Acts 2:4, Luke 22:12, Num 28:4, Dan 3:23); 'Exod. xx' as Ex 20:1 with a note; margin 'v. 14' there is Acts 1:14. Matt 17:19 / Luke 17:6: 'Tollere, et jacta te in mare' fits Matt 21:21 (note). Notes: 2 Esd 9:3 'quater in nocte' not in the Vulgate; Mark 14:40 'præ tristitia' is from Luke 22:45; Ecclus 27:30 adds 'illusio'; Prov 18:1 exsecrabilis. DR data slip: 1 John 5:4 'overcameth'.

Part 1 of 2 published (scheduled run, two workers split at the v. 10 lemma; Dan 7:1 to the end of v. 23, '…munitiones comburendo', taking the first line of daniel-008-part2.txt to finish the sentence). Part 2 (published earlier) also began with 'Et conculcabit … comburendo': that duplicate paragraph was removed. Misread margins corrected with notes: 'Ps. lxxxix, 14' = Ps 79:14; 'Ps. xxxiv, 6' = Ps 33:6; 'Apoc. iv, 2, i' = Apoc 4:2, 4; 'I Cor. xv' = 1 Cor 15:24; 'Eccle. iii, 20' (Jerome's wording closer to Ecclus 40:11) reference-only. Is 10:23/Rom 9:28: Rom marked, Is reference-only. Deut 32:8 quoted after the Septuagint (noted). Apoc 19:20 loosely quoted (noted). Matt 19:27 words ('Vos qui reliquistis omnia') unmarked, no margin note (noted). Kept as printed with notes: 'ad labores ac verba' (perhaps verbera), Nahum 'faciem consummationem' (faciet). DR data slip: Is 8:8 'the breadth of thy, land'.

Part 2 published (22:25 run, translated directly; Dan 7:23 'Et conculcabit' to the middle of the Apoc 12:10 quotation, 4 paragraphs). It starts at 'runt. Et conculcabit': the word 'nocue-runt' at the end of daniel-008-part1.txt belongs to part 1. Needs scan of PDF 124 (printed p. 114): the transcription of that page has only a few lines, so the end of the article (after 'et potestas Christi', Apoc 12:10, and Dan 7:28) is missing, marked […] with a note. Pages given as pp. 101–114 for the whole article. Matt 12:8 and John 14:6 reference-only (paraphrased); notes on Denis's readings 'sermones blasphemiæ' (v. 25), 'Data est bestiæ' (Apoc 13:7), 'ejus' (Apoc 14:11).

Re-cut (22:25 run): the old daniel-009 was not an article but the heading and first sentence of Art. X (ch. 9, running heads 'ART. X'); Art. IX (ch. 8; running heads PDF 124-133 'ENARRATIO IN CAP. VIII … ART. IX') had been left inside daniel-008-part2.txt with no heading. daniel-009.txt now holds Art. IX. Needs scan of PDF 124 (printed p. 114): its transcription has only a few lines, so the end of Art. VIII (after 'Nunc facta est salus et virtus, et regnum Dei nostri, et potestas Christi', Apoc 12:10; Dan 7:28) and the heading and start of Art. IX (Dan 8:1 to the middle of v. 2, up to '…regione, id est in regno Elamitarum') are lost. The rest of Art. IX (PDF 124-133) reads clean and can be translated once p. 124 is supplied.

The article's first lines ('NUNC visio scribitur … In anno primo Darii filii Assueri', PDF p. 133 foot of left column under the heading) were cut into daniel-009.txt; they are included here. Margin 'Is. i, 10' read as Is 50:10; 'Oratio Manassæ' not in the DR text (reference to 2 Par 33:12, with a note); 'Matt. xvi, 4' is 16:3 in the DR text.

Published (22:25 run, two workers split at the v. 10 lemma). Notes: Ezech 1:16 'quasi visio maris' said of the wheels, not the creatures; Ezech 18:21 'Quacumque hora ingemuerit peccator' is not in the Vulgate (reference-only, 18:22 marked); Denis's readings 'juxta principem Persarum' (v. 13) and 'visio in dies protelatur' (v. 14). Margin variants kept as printed: 'accidereve' (margin 'accidere'), 'lauta ciboria' (probably cibaria), '*sermonem' (v. 1). Augustine's reading of Luke 10:42 ('Unum est opus') left unmarked with a note.

Published (scheduled run, two workers split at the v. 22 lemma). The article's last lines ('populos, et telam quam orditus est super universas nationes … Morere; et statim fulminabitur', PDF 168 right column) had been cut into daniel-013.txt (lines 27–45, before a repeated Art. XIII heading); they are now published at the end of Art. XII, so leave them out of Art. XIII (daniel-013 was claimed by another run when this was found). Margin 'Esther i, 1; 11, 18' taken as Esth 1:1 and 2:18 (reference only, noted); 'Dan. vi' as Dan 6:1; 'II Mach. ix, 7 et seq.' as 2 Mach 9:7 (noted: the pain is at 9:5). v. 10: Denis prints 'Et exaltabitur cornu ejus' as Scripture, not in the Vulgate of v. 10 (noted, unmarked). Variants noted: cornu for cor (v. 12), illum/illud (v. 17), coram eo (v. 26), impii testamentum simulabunt (v. 32), principes (v. 41), fortitudine with margin variant multitudine (v. 44). In Jerome's quotation in the introduction 'a capitulo duodecimo' kept as printed (perhaps decimo).

The transcription of PDF p. 168 put the end of Art. XII (right column top, 'populos, et telam quam orditus est … Morere; et statim fulminabitur.', with Jerome's LXX reading of Is 25:7 and the Scholastic History on Antichrist's death) inside daniel-013.txt; it was left out of Art. XIII and is missing from daniel-012.txt, so check that Art. XII has it. Margin notes giving only a chapter (4 Kings xxv, 2 Par. xxxvi, Gen. vi, vii) given as verse 1 with a note; Ezech 4:6 tagged though not in the margin (Denis names Ezechiel). Douay-Rheims slip in data/bible/drc John 6:45: 'cometh forth me' for 'cometh to me'. (Now published at the end of Art. XII by the Daniel 11 run.)

Published (22:30 run, two workers split at the v. 22 lemma). Corrected 'filium suam' → 'filiam suam' (v. 3). Margin '1 Reg. xv' taken as 1 Kings 15:27–28; 'Ps. x, 5, sec. Hebr.' as Ps 9:26 (note). Bar 1:19, 22 and Cant 2:4 ('Vulnerata caritate ego sum') reference-only with notes; '2 Kings 24:14' (Coarctor undique nimis) marked without margin note (Denis names Kings). Margin variants '⟦virtute⟧' (v. 1) dropped, '* adfleverunt' (v. 33) as a note. Denis's readings noted: Ecclus 1:22, 23:37, 9:8, the v. 17 lemma, 'in manus hominum' (v. 23), no 'sanctum' (v. 45). DR data slip: Dan 13:6 'all that hand any matters of judgment' (should be 'had').

Whole article published from this file (scheduled run, two workers split at the v. 18 lemma; Dan 14:1–42 and Jerome on the 'loud voice', ending 'Amen.', PDF p. 195 = p. 185). The transcription-failure message after 'Amen.' is PDF 196, which follows the end of the article (probably a blank verso). Margin verse numbers run one ahead from v. 8 (tagged by the text). 'Et rex Astyages' marked Dan 13:65 (no margin note). Jer 10:15/51:18: 51:18 marked, 10:15 reference-only; Jer 40:7–12 range noted. Variant notes '*Porro Daniel', '*Contemnebant', 'corallinis' given as notes; 'dirutus' (Vulgate diruptus) kept. 14:41 lemma's Latin side is in the Vulgate wording (Denis interposes a gloss).

Not part of Art. XV (scheduled run, 23 Nov): Art. XV ends on PDF 195 and was published whole. This file (PDF 197–208) is the front matter of the Minor Prophets (title pages, the Cologne editor's dedicatory letter to Johann Rinck, …), and PDF 200 and 206 failed to transcribe. Dave: decide whether any of it should be translated; otherwise mark done.
General preamble to the twelve Prophets, no verse tags. The first line has '[…]' after 'evangelicis' (probably nothing lost; kept as printed).
Margin '* novem' corrects Denis's 'viginti octo' (Ezechias' years) to 29: noted at 4 Kings 18:2.
Margin 'IV Reg. xxv, 24' does not fit (4 Kings 25:7 used, with a note); 'Ephes. v, 23' beside words of Col 1:18 (noted). DR text slip at Rom 9:26: 'it shalt be'.
Transcription of PDF 220–221 had ae/oe for æ/œ: normalized; 'affixerunt' read as 'afflixerunt'. Matt 7:23 quoted with the closing words of Luke 13:27 (noted).

(from the hosea-008 run, 22:43) hosea-007.txt stops mid-word at '…quorum conver-'. The rest of Art. VII stands in hosea-008.txt (lines 37–44, PDF p. 240): 'satio in cœlis est, exaudit pro se ipsis et aliis. Illi quoque exaudiunt terram, id est peccatores et pœnitentes, auxiliando eis pro posse in omnibus, utpote instruendo, orando, increpando, et gratiam sibi concessam, ipsis liberalissime impertiendo. — Postremo moralitas eorum quæ nunc omissa sunt, patet ex præcedenti articulo.' It is left out of Art. VIII; add it to the end of Art. VII.
